title: feat(react,vue): add onReady callback, ref forwarding, and container props

issue_comments.body:
### Code review

OpenSpec proposal, READMEs, and tests are all in place. A few lower-confidence concerns worth a look (none are individually blocking, but the first one is a real coordination problem):

1. **Direct overlap with the still-open PR #17.** Both PRs add `onReady` to `packages/react/src/use-editor.ts`, `packages/react/src/types.ts`, `packages/vue/src/use-editor.ts`, and `packages/vue/src/types.ts`, and both claim Roadmap item #4. Whichever lands second will need a non-trivial rebase. The two also disagree on call-site shape — PR #19 destructures `onReady` out of config before passing to `createEditor` (cleaner, prevents leakage), while PR #17 passes the full config through. Worth coordinating which approach lands.

2. **Vue `<Editor>` spreads `...attrs` into `UseEditorConfig` without setting `inheritAttrs: false`.** Result: any non-prop attribute (`class`, `style`, `id`, `data-*`, parent event listeners) is BOTH spread into `createEditor` as an `EditorConfig` field AND auto-applied to the root `<div>` via Vue's default attribute inheritance. The forwarded keys silently pollute `EditorConfig` (today they're ignored; if `EditorConfig` later grows a field named like a DOM attribute, this becomes a real collision). Suggested fix: declare `inheritAttrs: false` and explicitly list which attrs forward where, OR drop the `...attrs` spread entirely and stick to the declared `initialValue` + `className` props plus the `ready` emit.

https://github.com/floatboatai/Nexus-Editor/blob/678181bde049ba4e3ff26198a51dba627884d27a/packages/vue/src/editor.ts#L1-L40

3. **Vue `className` prop is non-idiomatic.** Vue users will reasonably write `<Editor class="foo" />` — that goes through `attrs` (issue #2 above) rather than `props.className`, so the explicit className handling never fires. Either rename the prop to `class` (the framework will merge it onto the root automatically), or document that consumers must use `class-name="foo"` and remove the auto-attr-inheritance side channel.

4. **React `useImperativeHandle(ref, () => editor as EditorAPI, [editor])` casts a possibly-null value.** `editor` comes from `useState<EditorAPI | null>(null)` and is null on the first render — the `as EditorAPI` cast hides this from the type system. Consumers writing `ref.current.focus()` without a null-check will crash on the first paint frame. Either change the type to `EditorAPI | null` (and update the spec scenario) or use the synchronous `editorRef.current` rather than the state.

https://github.com/floatboatai/Nexus-Editor/blob/678181bde049ba4e3ff26198a51dba627884d27a/packages/react/src/editor.tsx

5. **React StrictMode double-mount fires `onReady` twice, violating the spec's "exactly once" guarantee.** In React 18 dev, the mount effect runs → cleanup destroys the instance and nulls `editorRef.current` → effect runs again → `createEditor` is called a second time → `onReady` fires again with a fresh instance. The first instance is destroyed; consumers who captured it via the first `onReady` call hold a dead handle. The `react-sdk/spec.md` scenario says `onReady` SHALL be called exactly once. Consider a `useRef` flag to guard the second invocation, or relax the spec to "exactly once per editor instance".

https://github.com/floatboatai/Nexus-Editor/blob/678181bde049ba4e3ff26198a51dba627884d27a/packages/react/src/use-editor.ts

6. **Vue test "exposes editor via template ref" only asserts the `ready` event, not the exposed `editor` ref.** The test name promises one thing; the assertion checks another. Add an assertion against `wrapper.vm.editor` (or the equivalent expose surface).

7. Process nit: PR adds new `use-editor.test.tsx` / `use-editor.test.ts` files alongside the pre-existing `editor-react.test.tsx` / `editor-vue.test.ts` without removing or merging them. Two test files with overlapping mount/destroy cases will diverge over time.
